# SSGOI setup guide

SSGOI adds route transitions without replacing the application router.

Current core version: `@ssgoi/core@7.0.0-beta.2`

This file is the React/Next.js setup plus an index. Deep topics live in their
own files — fetch one only when its topic applies:

- Effect options and variants: `https://ssgoi.dev/llms/<effect>.txt` (table below)
- Persistent nav / complex routing: https://ssgoi.dev/llms/bottom-nav.txt
- Other frameworks: `https://ssgoi.dev/llms/<framework>.txt` (table below)
- Mechanism and debugging: https://ssgoi.dev/llms/how-it-works.txt

## Setup

### 1. Install

```bash
npm install @ssgoi/react
```

### 2. Provider

One config, one `<Ssgoi>`, above all routed content. One rule is enough to
start:

```tsx
// app/ssgoi-provider.tsx
"use client";

import { type ReactNode } from "react";
import { Ssgoi } from "@ssgoi/react";
import { drill } from "@ssgoi/react/view-transitions";

const config = {
  transitions: [{ on: "/**", except: "/", transition: drill() }],
};

export function SsgoiProvider({ children }: { children: ReactNode }) {
  return <Ssgoi config={config}>{children}</Ssgoi>;
}
```

`transitions` also accepts `({ isMobile }) => rules` to branch mobile/desktop:

```ts
transitions: ({ isMobile }) =>
  isMobile
    ? [{ on: "/**", except: "/", transition: drill() }]
    : [{ priority: -100, on: "/**", transition: fade() }],
```

Scroll behavior is derived from each matched rule. The automatic policy and
exact override are covered in Scroll restoration and middleware below.

### 3. Layout shell

```tsx
// app/layout.tsx
import { type ReactNode } from "react";
import { SsgoiProvider } from "./ssgoi-provider";

export default function RootLayout({ children }: { children: ReactNode }) {
  return (
    <html lang="en">
      <body>
        <main className="relative z-0 min-h-dvh overflow-x-clip">
          <SsgoiProvider>{children}</SsgoiProvider>
        </main>
      </body>
    </html>
  );
}
```

The three classes are required, on the element around `<Ssgoi>`:

| class | role |
| --- | --- |
| `relative` | containing block for the leaving page (re-inserted with `position: absolute`) |
| `z-0` | stacking context so the leaving page stays above the shell background |
| `overflow-x-clip` | no horizontal scrollbar flash during slide/drill-style motion |

Mechanism: https://ssgoi.dev/llms/how-it-works.txt

### 4. Route boundary

The base pattern — pathname as both React key and transition id:

```tsx
// app/ssgoi-route-boundary.tsx
"use client";

import { type ReactNode } from "react";
import { usePathname } from "next/navigation";

export function SsgoiRouteBoundary({ children }: { children: ReactNode }) {
  const pathname = usePathname();

  return (
    <div key={pathname} data-ssgoi-transition={pathname}>
      {children}
    </div>
  );
}

// app/layout.tsx — wrap the provider's children
<SsgoiProvider>
  <SsgoiRouteBoundary>{children}</SsgoiRouteBoundary>
</SsgoiProvider>
```

The principle: a changed `key` makes React unmount the routed region and mount
the new one — that unmount/mount pair is what SSGOI animates.
`data-ssgoi-transition` is the id that rules match. Put the boundary once in a
layout and every navigation under it transitions.

(Deprecated: `<SsgoiTransition>` only rendered this attribute — set it
directly.)

### 5. Verify

1. Navigate `/` → any page: the new page slides in from the right.
2. Navigate back: it slides back out.
3. No animation, or the wrong region moves → Troubleshooting below.

## Choosing transitions

One row = one decision: the effect, the rule form to write it with, and the
file with full options and variants.

| UX intent | transition | rule form | options |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| default / unrelated pages | `fade()` | `priority: -100, on: "/**"` | https://ssgoi.dev/llms/fade.txt |
| list → detail, drilling deeper | `drill()` | `on` + `except` | https://ssgoi.dev/llms/drill.txt |
| tabs / steps with left-right order | `slide()` | `ordered` | https://ssgoi.dev/llms/slide.txt |
| sibling pages, Material shared-axis | `axis()` | `ordered` | https://ssgoi.dev/llms/axis.txt |
| compose / filters / modal-like route | `sheet()` | `from`/`to` | https://ssgoi.dev/llms/sheet.txt |
| card or image expands to detail | `zoom()` | `from`/`to` | https://ssgoi.dev/llms/zoom.txt |
| shared element across two pages | `hero()` | `from`/`to` | https://ssgoi.dev/llms/hero.txt |
| vertical sequence / editorial paging | `scroll()` | `ordered` | https://ssgoi.dev/llms/scroll.txt |

Stylistic effects (any rule form): `film`, `strip`, `rotate`, `blind`,
`jaemin` — each at `https://ssgoi.dev/llms/<name>.txt`.

## Route rules

| form | meaning | direction |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `on` (+ `except`) | route family | entering = forward, leaving = backward |
| `from` / `to` | exact pair | as written = forward; reversed by default |
| `ordered: [...]` | both routes in the list | increasing index = forward |

| pattern | matches |
| --- | --- |
| `/posts` | exactly `/posts` |
| `/posts/*` | exactly one extra segment |
| `/posts/**` | `/posts` and every descendant |

`priority`: higher wins before path specificity; ties resolve by specificity,
then declaration order. A bare `*` is a compatibility alias for `/**`.

## Persistent nav and complex routing

The situation: some pages share a bottom nav, some don't. Tab → tab must keep
the nav still; tab → detail must send the nav away with the page.

```text
app/
  layout.tsx                 # one provider + outer "app-shell" boundary
  (main)/
    layout.tsx               # inner content boundary + the common BottomNav
    page.tsx  collections/page.tsx  create/page.tsx
  (detail)/
    photo/[id]/page.tsx      # no nav
```

The pathname-keyed boundary can't do this — its key changes on every
navigation, so the nav remounts every time. What to achieve instead is a key
scope:

- The boundary `id` is always the real route.
- The outer boundary's `key` stays constant (e.g. `"main-shell"`) while the
  route is inside `(main)` — tab → tab keeps the shell and nav mounted — and
  falls back to the pathname outside it, so entering or leaving the shell
  transitions the whole shell, nav included.
- An inner boundary keyed on the pathname sits above the nav and owns
  tab → tab transitions.

```text
┌─ outer boundary (key: "main-shell" inside (main)) ─────┐
│  ┌─ inner boundary (key: pathname) ─────────────────┐  │
│  │  tab page                                        │  │
│  └──────────────────────────────────────────────────┘  │
│  BottomNav (persistent, outside the inner boundary)    │
└────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┘

tab → tab     : inner boundary remounts · nav stays
tab → detail  : outer boundary remounts · nav leaves with it
detail → tab  : outer boundary re-enters with the nav
```

Full pattern — resolver code, modal/intercepted routes, pitfalls:
https://ssgoi.dev/llms/bottom-nav.txt

## Scroll restoration and middleware

Scroll behavior follows the matched route relationship automatically:

- `on`: restore the forward `from` side outside the scope; reset the `to` side
  matched by `on`.
- `from`/`to`: restore `from`; reset `to`.
- `ordered`: restore both sides.

The policy is chosen per navigation, so the same path can restore under one
rule and reset under another. The outgoing page always keeps its current scroll
through its OUT animation. Reset or restoration happens only when a page
becomes IN.

```ts
const config = {
  // rewrite (from, to) before rule matching, e.g. strip a locale prefix
  middleware: (from, to) => ({
    from: from.replace(/^\/(en|ko)/, ""),
    to: to.replace(/^\/(en|ko)/, ""),
  }),
  transitions: [
    {
      on: "/posts/**",
      except: "/posts",
      transition: drill(),
    },
    {
      ordered: ["/tabs/feed", "/tabs/search", "/tabs/profile"],
      transition: slide(),
    },
    // Exact override: preserve both sides of this pair.
    {
      from: "/gallery",
      to: "/photo/*",
      preserveScroll: { from: true, to: true },
      transition: zoom(),
    },
  ],
};
```

`preserveScroll.from` and `.to` always describe the rule's semantic forward
relationship. Backward navigation reverses their physical OUT/IN mapping. For
an `on` rule, paths outside the scope are semantic `from`, paths inside are
semantic `to`, and an inside-to-inside navigation applies `to` to both pages.
Use `preserveScroll: { from: boolean, to: boolean }` only to replace the
automatic policy. For `ordered`, the lower-index side is semantic `from` and
the higher-index side is semantic `to`. There is no separate mobile scroll
default; a functional `transitions({ isMobile })` config simply supplies the
active rules whose policies are resolved.

## Troubleshooting

- No animation: both routes inside one `<Ssgoi>`; both DOM nodes carry
  `data-ssgoi-transition`; a rule matches both paths.
- Wrong region animates: find the nearest boundary whose key changed; keep
  persistent UI outside the inner boundary; fix the key scope so routes in
  the same shell share a key.
- Jumps or flickers: shell classes from Setup 3; full-height background on
  route boundaries.

Mechanism deep-dive: https://ssgoi.dev/llms/how-it-works.txt

Runnable templates:
https://github.com/meursyphus/ssgoi/tree/main/templates
(nextjs · react-router · tanstack-router · sveltekit · nuxt · solidstart · qwik)
